title: My Coworker Stole My Homemade Cake. Then 14 People Asked for a Recipe I Didn't Remember Making (PART 2)

blocks.text: The restaurant owner's name was André Fontaine. His grandfather, Louis, had opened their restaurant in New Orleans in 1951. In 1968, a fire destroyed the kitchen. The fire marshal blamed a young pastry cook who'd left an oven on overnight. She was fired, and her name was dragged through the neighborhood. Then she left town and was never heard from again.

The second "recipe" wasn't a recipe at all. André recognized it as the kind of code cooks in his grandfather's kitchen used to pass notes: the first letter of each ingredient spelled out words. We worked through it on the phone, line by line. "Molasses. Raisins. Allspice. Yeast…"
It spelled out a sentence: "MR. ROUX LIT IT FOR THE INSURANCE. I SAVED THE BOOK."
Mr. Roux had been Louis Fontaine's business partner.

André went very quiet. His family had always suspected something was wrong about the fire. Roux had left the partnership two months later with a large insurance payout and opened his own restaurant across town.

My aunt hadn't stolen the recipe book. She'd grabbed it from the burning kitchen and run. She knew no one would believe a twenty-year-old Black pastry cook over a white business owner in 1968, so she copied the most important recipes into her own notebook, wrote her message in the only code she knew Louis would recognize, and moved to Texas. She'd hoped someday the notebook would find its way back.
She never married. She died in 2019 and left me the notebook because I was the only one in the family who baked.
André flew to Austin with his father. When they saw her handwriting, his father cried.
Louis had died believing Josephine was responsible. André told me his grandfather used to say she was the most talented baker he ever hired, and that it broke his heart to believe she'd betrayed him.

The Fontaine family published the story in their local paper, with my aunt's photograph. Their chocolate cake, the one Melissa passed off as her own, is back on their menu now, under a new name: "Josephine's Cake."
Melissa apologized. Eventually. I gave her the recipe. I left out the spice that makes it work.
